plain_description.what: A planned battery of checks on the rebuilt version 2 tree, which is built on a cleaner data split with no repeated question text. The tree is rebuilt several times to see whether it comes out the same, whether it files new questions correctly, whether it beats class-aware k-means and a flat mixture, whether its cells change the model-choice policy, and whether it has a statistically certified top-level split.
plain_description.why: The thesis needs a tree that is reproducible and better than simpler groupings before any per-cell claim can rest on it.
plain_description.information: If the tree passes, it becomes a stable, defensible base for the later per-cell tests. If it fails, the thesis has to work with a simpler partition. Result: run, but the post-run review has not happened yet. The first gate, byte-for-byte reproducibility, FAILED as registered, so the lane stopped. The tree structure itself reproduces exactly. The failure came from the order of queries inside a node (a multi-threaded step) and from order-sensitive metrics. None of the other checks (filing, k-means comparison, flat mixture, policy, certificate, order stability) was read. A follow-up run is planned.
